<hr /><a id="class-domwordsiterator"></a>
<h3>Class: DOMWordsIterator</h3></li>
</ul>
<blockquote>
<p>Iterates individual words of DOM text and CDATA nodes while keeping track of their position in the document. Example: $doc = new DOMDocument(); $doc-&gt;load('example.xml'); foreach(new DOMWordsIterator($doc) as $word) echo $word;</p>
</blockquote>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Visibility</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>__construct(</strong><em><a href="http://php.net/manual/en/class.domnode.php">\DOMNode</a></em> <strong>$el</strong>)</strong> : <em>void</em><br /><em>expects DOMElement or DOMDocument (see DOMDocument::load and DOMDocument::loadHTML)</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>current()</strong> : <em>string/null</em><br /><em>Return the current element</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>currentElement()</strong> : <em>\DOMElement/null</em><br /><em>Returns DOMElement that is currently being iterated or NULL if iterator has finished.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>currentWordPosition()</strong> : <em>array</em><br /><em>Returns position in text as DOMText node and character offset. (it's NOT a byte offset, you must use mb_substr() or similar to use this offset properly). node may be NULL if iterator has finished.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>key()</strong> : <em>int/null</em><br /><em>Return the key of the current element</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>next()</strong> : <em>void</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>rewind()</strong> : <em>void</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>valid()</strong> : <em>bool</em><br /><em>Checks if current position is valid</em></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><em>This class implements \Iterator, \Traversable</em></p>
<p><hr /><a id="class-domlettersiterator"></a></p>
<h3>Class: DOMLettersIterator</h3>
<blockquote>
<p>Iterates individual characters (Unicode codepoints) of DOM text and CDATA nodes while keeping track of their position in the document. Example: $doc = new DOMDocument(); $doc-&gt;load('example.xml'); foreach(new DOMLettersIterator($doc) as $letter) echo $letter; NB: If you only need characters without their position in the document, use DOMNode-&gt;textContent instead.</p>
</blockquote>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Visibility</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>__construct(</strong><em><a href="http://php.net/manual/en/class.domnode.php">\DOMNode</a></em> <strong>$el</strong>)</strong> : <em>void</em><br /><em>expects DOMElement or DOMDocument (see DOMDocument::load and DOMDocument::loadHTML)</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>current()</strong> : <em>string/null</em><br /><em>Return the current element</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>currentElement()</strong> : <em>\DOMElement/null</em><br /><em>Returns DOMElement that is currently being iterated or NULL if iterator has finished.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>currentTextPosition()</strong> : <em>array</em><br /><em>Returns position in text as DOMText node and character offset. (it's NOT a byte offset, you must use mb_substr() or similar to use this offset properly). node may be NULL if iterator has finished.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>key()</strong> : <em>int/null</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>next()</strong> : <em>void</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>rewind()</strong> : <em>void</em></td>
</tr>

<p><hr /><a id="class-gravcommontaxonomy"></a></p>
<h3>Class: \Grav\Common\Taxonomy</h3>
<blockquote>
<p>The Taxonomy object is a singleton that holds a reference to a 'taxonomy map'. This map is constructed as a multidimensional array. uses the taxonomy defined in the site.yaml file and is built when the page objects are recursed. Basically every time a page is found that has taxonomy references, an entry to the page is stored in the taxonomy map.  The map has the following format: [taxonomy_type][taxonomy_value][page_path] For example: [category][blog][path/to/item1] [tag][grav][path/to/item1] [tag][grav][path/to/item2] [tag][dog][path/to/item3]</p>
</blockquote>

</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>addTaxonomy(</strong><em><a href="#interface-gravcommonpageinterfacespageinterface">\Grav\Common\Page\Interfaces\PageInterface</a></em> <strong>$page</strong>, <em>array/null</em> <strong>$page_taxonomy=null</strong>)</strong> : <em>void</em><br /><em>Takes an individual page and processes the taxonomies configured in its header. It then adds those taxonomies to the map</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>

If you need to uppercase all the words you just have to pass 'all' as a second parameter. instead of just the first one.</em></td>

<td style="text-align: left;">public static</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>init()</strong> : <em>void</em></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public static</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>pluralize(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$word</strong>, <em>int</em> <strong>$count=2</strong>)</strong> : <em>string/false Plural noun</em><br /><em>Pluralizes English nouns.</em></td>

</tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">public static</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>tableize(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$class_name</strong>)</strong> : <em>string plural_table_name</em><br /><em>Converts a class name to its table name according to rails naming conventions. Converts &quot;Person&quot; to &quot;people&quot;</em></td>

<td style="text-align: left;">public static</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>titleize(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$word</strong>, <em>string</em> <strong>$uppercase=<code>''</code></strong>)</strong> : <em>string Text formatted as title</em><br /><em>Converts an underscored or CamelCase word into a English sentence. The titleize public function converts text like &quot;WelcomePage&quot;, &quot;welcome_page&quot; or  &quot;welcome page&quot; to this &quot;Welcome Page&quot;. If second parameter is set to 'first' it will only capitalize the first character of the title. first character. Otherwise it will uppercase all the words in the title.</em></td>

  $media-&gt;copyUploadedFile($uploadedFile, $filename);</code></pre>

<pre><code>`$langCode = null; $referrer = $pages-&gt;referrerRoute($langCode, '/admin');` returns relative referrer url within /admin and updates $langCode`$langCode = 'en'; $referrer = $pages-&gt;referrerRoute($langCode, '/admin');` returns relative referrer url within the /en/admin</code></pre>

<h6>Examples of AbstractMedia::checkUploadedFile()</h6>
<pre><code>$filename = null;  // Override filename if needed (ignored if randomizing filenames).
  $settings = ['destination' =&gt; 'user://pages/media']; // Settings from the form field.
  $filename = $media-&gt;checkUploadedFile($uploadedFile, $filename, $settings);
  $media-&gt;copyUploadedFile($uploadedFile, $filename);</code></pre>
<h6>Examples of AbstractMedia::copyUploadedFile()</h6>
<pre><code>$settings = ['destination' =&gt; 'user://pages/media']; // Settings from the form field.
  $filename = $media-&gt;checkUploadedFile($uploadedFile, $filename, $settings);
  $media-&gt;copyUploadedFile($uploadedFile, $filename, $settings);</code></pre>

<h3>Interface: \Grav\Framework\File\Interfaces\FileInterface</h3>
<blockquote>
<p>Defines common interface for all file readers. File readers allow you to read and optionally write files of various file formats, such as:</p>
</blockquote>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Visibility</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>delete()</strong> : <em>bool Returns <code>true</code> if the file was successfully deleted, <code>false</code> otherwise.</em><br /><em>Delete file from filesystem.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>exists()</strong> : <em>bool Returns <code>true</code> if the filename exists and is a regular file, <code>false</code> otherwise.</em><br /><em>Check if the file exits in the filesystem.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getBasename()</strong> : <em>string Returns basename of the file.</em><br /><em>Get basename of the file (filename without the associated file extension).</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getCreationTime()</strong> : <em>int Returns Unix timestamp. If file does not exist, method returns current time.</em><br /><em>Get file creation time.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getExtension(</strong><em>bool</em> <strong>$withDot=false</strong>)</strong> : <em>string Returns file extension of the file (can be empty).</em><br /><em>Get file extension of the file.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getFilePath()</strong> : <em>string Returns path and filename in the filesystem. Can also be URI.</em><br /><em>Get both path and filename of the file.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getFilename()</strong> : <em>string Returns name of the file.</em><br /><em>Get filename of the file.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getModificationTime()</strong> : <em>int Returns Unix timestamp. If file does not exist, method returns current time.</em><br /><em>Get file modification time.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getPath()</strong> : <em>string Returns path in the filesystem. Can also be URI.</em><br /><em>Get path of the file.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>isLocked()</strong> : <em>bool Returns <code>true</code> if the file is locked, <code>false</code> otherwise.</em><br /><em>Returns true if file has been locked by you for writing.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>isReadable()</strong> : <em>bool Returns <code>true</code> if the file can be read, <code>false</code> otherwise.</em><br /><em>Check if file exists and can be read.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>isWritable()</strong> : <em>bool Returns <code>true</code> if the file can be written, <code>false</code> otherwise.</em><br /><em>Check if file can be written.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>load()</strong> : <em>string/array/object/false Returns file content or <code>false</code> if file couldn't be read.</em><br /><em>(Re)Load a file and return file contents.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>lock(</strong><em>bool</em> <strong>$block=true</strong>)</strong> : <em>bool Returns <code>true</code> if the file was successfully locked, <code>false</code> otherwise.</em><br /><em>Lock file for writing. You need to manually call unlock().</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>rename(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$path</strong>)</strong> : <em>bool Returns <code>true</code> if the file was successfully renamed, <code>false</code> otherwise.</em><br /><em>Rename file in the filesystem if it exists. Target folder will be created if if did not exist.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>save(</strong><em>mixed</em> <strong>$data</strong>)</strong> : <em>void</em><br /><em>Save file. See supported data format for each of the file format.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>unlock()</strong> : <em>bool Returns <code>true</code> if the file was successfully unlocked, <code>false</code> otherwise.</em><br /><em>Unlock file after writing.</em></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract getAuthority()</strong> : <em>string The URI authority, in &quot;[user-info@]host[:port]&quot; format.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the authority component of the URI. If no authority information is present, this method MUST return an empty string. The authority syntax of the URI is: <pre></em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract getFragment()</strong> : <em>string The URI fragment.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the fragment component of the URI. If no fragment is present, this method MUST return an empty string. The leading &quot;#&quot; character is not part of the fragment and MUST NOT be added. The value returned MUST be percent-encoded, but MUST NOT double-encode any characters. To determine what characters to encode, please refer to RFC 3986, Sections 2 and 3.5.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract getHost()</strong> : <em>string The URI host.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the host component of the URI. If no host is present, this method MUST return an empty string. The value returned MUST be normalized to lowercase, per RFC 3986 Section 3.2.2.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract getPath()</strong> : <em>string The URI path.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the path component of the URI. The path can either be empty or absolute (starting with a slash) or rootless (not starting with a slash). Implementations MUST support all three syntaxes. Normally, the empty path &quot;&quot; and absolute path &quot;/&quot; are considered equal as defined in RFC 7230 Section 2.7.3. But this method MUST NOT automatically do this normalization because in contexts with a trimmed base path, e.g. the front controller, this difference becomes significant. It's the task of the user to handle both &quot;&quot; and &quot;/&quot;. The value returned MUST be percent-encoded, but MUST NOT double-encode any characters. To determine what characters to encode, please refer to RFC 3986, Sections 2 and 3.3. As an example, if the value should include a slash (&quot;/&quot;) not intended as delimiter between path segments, that value MUST be passed in encoded form (e.g., &quot;%2F&quot;) to the instance.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract getPort()</strong> : <em>null/int The URI port.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the port component of the URI. If a port is present, and it is non-standard for the current scheme, this method MUST return it as an integer. If the port is the standard port used with the current scheme, this method SHOULD return null. If no port is present, and no scheme is present, this method MUST return a null value. If no port is present, but a scheme is present, this method MAY return the standard port for that scheme, but SHOULD return null.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract getQuery()</strong> : <em>string The URI query string.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the query string of the URI. If no query string is present, this method MUST return an empty string. The leading &quot;?&quot; character is not part of the query and MUST NOT be added. The value returned MUST be percent-encoded, but MUST NOT double-encode any characters. To determine what characters to encode, please refer to RFC 3986, Sections 2 and 3.4. As an example, if a value in a key/value pair of the query string should include an ampersand (&quot;&amp;&quot;) not intended as a delimiter between values, that value MUST be passed in encoded form (e.g., &quot;%26&quot;) to the instance.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract getScheme()</strong> : <em>string The URI scheme.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the scheme component of the URI. If no scheme is present, this method MUST return an empty string. The value returned MUST be normalized to lowercase, per RFC 3986 Section 3.1. The trailing &quot;:&quot; character is not part of the scheme and MUST NOT be added.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract getUserInfo()</strong> : <em>string The URI user information, in &quot;username[:password]&quot; format.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the user information component of the URI. If no user information is present, this method MUST return an empty string. If a user is present in the URI, this will return that value; additionally, if the password is also present, it will be appended to the user value, with a colon (&quot;:&quot;) separating the values. The trailing &quot;@&quot; character is not part of the user information and MUST NOT be added.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract withFragment(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$fragment</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified fragment.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified URI fragment. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified URI fragment. Users can provide both encoded and decoded fragment characters. Implementations ensure the correct encoding as outlined in getFragment(). An empty fragment value is equivalent to removing the fragment.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract withHost(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$host</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified host.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified host. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified host. An empty host value is equivalent to removing the host.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract withPath(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$path</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified path.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified path. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified path. The path can either be empty or absolute (starting with a slash) or rootless (not starting with a slash). Implementations MUST support all three syntaxes. If the path is intended to be domain-relative rather than path relative then it must begin with a slash (&quot;/&quot;). Paths not starting with a slash (&quot;/&quot;) are assumed to be relative to some base path known to the application or consumer. Users can provide both encoded and decoded path characters. Implementations ensure the correct encoding as outlined in getPath().</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract withPort(</strong><em>null/int/int</em> <strong>$port</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified port.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified port. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified port. Implementations MUST raise an exception for ports outside the established TCP and UDP port ranges. A null value provided for the port is equivalent to removing the port information. removes the port information.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract withQuery(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$query</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified query string.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified query string. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified query string. Users can provide both encoded and decoded query characters. Implementations ensure the correct encoding as outlined in getQuery(). An empty query string value is equivalent to removing the query string.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract withScheme(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$scheme</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified scheme.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified scheme. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified scheme. Implementations MUST support the schemes &quot;http&quot; and &quot;https&quot; case insensitively, and MAY accommodate other schemes if required. An empty scheme is equivalent to removing the scheme.</em></td>
</tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>abstract withUserInfo(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$user</strong>, <em>null/string/string</em> <strong>$password=null</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified user information.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified user information. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified user information. Password is optional, but the user information MUST include the user; an empty string for the user is equivalent to removing user information.</em></td>

<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>isAbsolute()</strong> : <em>bool</em><br /><em>Whether the URI is absolute, i.e. it has a scheme. An instance of UriInterface can either be an absolute URI or a relative reference. This method returns true if it is the former. An absolute URI has a scheme. A relative reference is used to express a URI relative to another URI, the base URI. Relative references can be divided into several forms: - network-path references, e.g. '//example.com/path' - absolute-path references, e.g. '/path' - relative-path references, e.g. 'subpath'</em></td>

<p><hr /><a id="class-gravframeworkuriuri"></a></p>
<h3>Class: \Grav\Framework\Uri\Uri</h3>
<blockquote>
<p>Implements PSR-7 UriInterface.</p>
</blockquote>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Visibility</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Function</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>__construct(</strong><em>array</em> <strong>$parts=array()</strong>)</strong> : <em>void</em><br /><em>You can use <code>UriFactory</code> functions to create new <code>Uri</code> objects.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getAuthority()</strong> : <em>string The URI authority, in &quot;[user-info@]host[:port]&quot; format.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the authority component of the URI. If no authority information is present, this method MUST return an empty string. The authority syntax of the URI is: <pre></em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getBaseUrl()</strong> : <em>string</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getFragment()</strong> : <em>string The URI fragment.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the fragment component of the URI. If no fragment is present, this method MUST return an empty string. The leading &quot;#&quot; character is not part of the fragment and MUST NOT be added. The value returned MUST be percent-encoded, but MUST NOT double-encode any characters. To determine what characters to encode, please refer to RFC 3986, Sections 2 and 3.5.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getHost()</strong> : <em>string The URI host.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the host component of the URI. If no host is present, this method MUST return an empty string. The value returned MUST be normalized to lowercase, per RFC 3986 Section 3.2.2.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getParts()</strong> : <em>array</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getPassword()</strong> : <em>string</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getPath()</strong> : <em>string The URI path.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the path component of the URI. The path can either be empty or absolute (starting with a slash) or rootless (not starting with a slash). Implementations MUST support all three syntaxes. Normally, the empty path &quot;&quot; and absolute path &quot;/&quot; are considered equal as defined in RFC 7230 Section 2.7.3. But this method MUST NOT automatically do this normalization because in contexts with a trimmed base path, e.g. the front controller, this difference becomes significant. It's the task of the user to handle both &quot;&quot; and &quot;/&quot;. The value returned MUST be percent-encoded, but MUST NOT double-encode any characters. To determine what characters to encode, please refer to RFC 3986, Sections 2 and 3.3. As an example, if the value should include a slash (&quot;/&quot;) not intended as delimiter between path segments, that value MUST be passed in encoded form (e.g., &quot;%2F&quot;) to the instance.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getPort()</strong> : <em>null/int The URI port.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the port component of the URI. If a port is present, and it is non-standard for the current scheme, this method MUST return it as an integer. If the port is the standard port used with the current scheme, this method SHOULD return null. If no port is present, and no scheme is present, this method MUST return a null value. If no port is present, but a scheme is present, this method MAY return the standard port for that scheme, but SHOULD return null.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getQuery()</strong> : <em>string The URI query string.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the query string of the URI. If no query string is present, this method MUST return an empty string. The leading &quot;?&quot; character is not part of the query and MUST NOT be added. The value returned MUST be percent-encoded, but MUST NOT double-encode any characters. To determine what characters to encode, please refer to RFC 3986, Sections 2 and 3.4. As an example, if a value in a key/value pair of the query string should include an ampersand (&quot;&amp;&quot;) not intended as a delimiter between values, that value MUST be passed in encoded form (e.g., &quot;%26&quot;) to the instance.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getQueryParam(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$key</strong>)</strong> : <em>string/null</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getQueryParams()</strong> : <em>array</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getScheme()</strong> : <em>string The URI scheme.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the scheme component of the URI. If no scheme is present, this method MUST return an empty string. The value returned MUST be normalized to lowercase, per RFC 3986 Section 3.1. The trailing &quot;:&quot; character is not part of the scheme and MUST NOT be added.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getUrl()</strong> : <em>string</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getUser()</strong> : <em>string</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>getUserInfo()</strong> : <em>string The URI user information, in &quot;username[:password]&quot; format.</em><br /><em>Retrieve the user information component of the URI. If no user information is present, this method MUST return an empty string. If a user is present in the URI, this will return that value; additionally, if the password is also present, it will be appended to the user value, with a colon (&quot;:&quot;) separating the values. The trailing &quot;@&quot; character is not part of the user information and MUST NOT be added.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>isAbsolute()</strong> : <em>bool</em><br /><em>Whether the URI is absolute, i.e. it has a scheme. An instance of UriInterface can either be an absolute URI or a relative reference. This method returns true if it is the former. An absolute URI has a scheme. A relative reference is used to express a URI relative to another URI, the base URI. Relative references can be divided into several forms: - network-path references, e.g. '//example.com/path' - absolute-path references, e.g. '/path' - relative-path references, e.g. 'subpath'</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>isAbsolutePathReference()</strong> : <em>bool</em><br /><em>Whether the URI is a absolute-path reference. A relative reference that begins with a single slash character is termed an absolute-path reference.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>isDefaultPort()</strong> : <em>bool</em><br /><em>Whether the URI has the default port of the current scheme. <code>$uri-&gt;getPort()</code> may return the standard port. This method can be used for some non-http/https Uri.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>isNetworkPathReference()</strong> : <em>bool</em><br /><em>Whether the URI is a network-path reference. A relative reference that begins with two slash characters is termed an network-path reference.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>isRelativePathReference()</strong> : <em>bool</em><br /><em>Whether the URI is a relative-path reference. A relative reference that does not begin with a slash character is termed a relative-path reference.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>isSameDocumentReference(</strong><em><a href="#class-gravframeworkuriuri">\Grav\Framework\Uri\Uri</a>Interface/null/\Psr\Http\Message\UriInterface</em> <strong>$base=null</strong>)</strong> : <em>bool</em><br /><em>Whether the URI is a same-document reference. A same-document reference refers to a URI that is, aside from its fragment component, identical to the base URI. When no base URI is given, only an empty URI reference (apart from its fragment) is considered a same-document reference.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>withFragment(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$fragment</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified fragment.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified URI fragment. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified URI fragment. Users can provide both encoded and decoded fragment characters. Implementations ensure the correct encoding as outlined in getFragment(). An empty fragment value is equivalent to removing the fragment.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>withHost(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$host</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified host.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified host. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified host. An empty host value is equivalent to removing the host.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>withPath(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$path</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified path.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified path. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified path. The path can either be empty or absolute (starting with a slash) or rootless (not starting with a slash). Implementations MUST support all three syntaxes. If the path is intended to be domain-relative rather than path relative then it must begin with a slash (&quot;/&quot;). Paths not starting with a slash (&quot;/&quot;) are assumed to be relative to some base path known to the application or consumer. Users can provide both encoded and decoded path characters. Implementations ensure the correct encoding as outlined in getPath().</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>withPort(</strong><em>null/int/int</em> <strong>$port</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified port.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified port. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified port. Implementations MUST raise an exception for ports outside the established TCP and UDP port ranges. A null value provided for the port is equivalent to removing the port information. removes the port information.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>withQuery(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$query</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified query string.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified query string. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified query string. Users can provide both encoded and decoded query characters. Implementations ensure the correct encoding as outlined in getQuery(). An empty query string value is equivalent to removing the query string.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>withQueryParam(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$key</strong>, <em>string/null</em> <strong>$value</strong>)</strong> : <em>\Psr\Http\Message\UriInterface</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>withQueryParams(</strong><em>array</em> <strong>$params</strong>)</strong> : <em>\Psr\Http\Message\UriInterface</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>withScheme(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$scheme</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified scheme.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified scheme. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified scheme. Implementations MUST support the schemes &quot;http&quot; and &quot;https&quot; case insensitively, and MAY accommodate other schemes if required. An empty scheme is equivalent to removing the scheme.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>withUserInfo(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$user</strong>, <em>null/string/string</em> <strong>$password=null</strong>)</strong> : <em>static A new instance with the specified user information.</em><br /><em>Return an instance with the specified user information. This method MUST retain the state of the current instance, and return an instance that contains the specified user information. Password is optional, but the user information MUST include the user; an empty string for the user is equivalent to removing user information.</em></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">public</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>withoutQueryParam(</strong><em>string</em> <strong>$key</strong>)</strong> : <em>\Psr\Http\Message\UriInterface</em></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
